properties.name: Five Suns — Aztec Creation Cycles
properties.summary: The Aztec cosmos underwent five creations (Suns), each destroyed by a different cataclysm. The first by jaguars, second by wind, third by fire-rain, fourth by flood. In the fifth (current) Sun, the humble god Nanahuatzin sacrificed himself by jumping into fire to become the sun, requiring blood sacrifice to maintain its movement.

properties.name: Quetzalcoatl's Exile
properties.summary: Quetzalcoatl, the Feathered Serpent, ruled as a wise priest-king of Tula. His rival Tezcatlipoca tricked him into drunkenness and sin. Ashamed, Quetzalcoatl exiled himself, sailing east on a raft of serpents, vowing to return. This prophecy later played into the Spanish conquest when Cortés was initially mistaken for the returning god.

properties.name: Tlaloc and the Rain Sacrifice
properties.summary: Tlaloc, the rain god, dwelt atop mountain peaks and in caves where clouds formed. He brought sustaining rain but also destructive storms, hail, and floods. Child sacrifices were offered to Tlaloc, their tears believed to bring rain. His paradise, Tlalocan, received those who died by water or lightning.

properties.name: Journey to Mictlan
properties.summary: After death, most Aztec souls traveled to Mictlan through nine challenging layers over four years. They crossed rivers of blood, passed between clashing mountains, endured razor-sharp winds, and finally stood before the death lord Mictlantecuhtli. A hairless dog (xoloitzcuintli) guided the soul through the underworld.

properties.name: Huitzilopochtli vs Coyolxauhqui
properties.summary: Coatlicue became pregnant from a ball of feathers. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui and 400 brothers plotted to kill her in shame. At the moment of attack, Huitzilopochtli was born fully armed, dismembering Coyolxauhqui and hurling her down Mount Coatepec. This battle is reenacted daily as the sun defeats the moon and stars.
